```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(jsonlite)
library(knitr)

raw_dir <- "raw_data"
main_file <- sort(list.files(raw_dir, pattern = "^main_.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE), decreasing = TRUE)[1]
pre_file <- sort(list.files(raw_dir, pattern = "^pre_experimental_.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE), decreasing = TRUE)[1]
page_file <- sort(list.files(raw_dir, pattern = "^PageTimes-.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE), decreasing = TRUE)[1]

if (any(is.na(c(main_file, pre_file, page_file)))) {
  stop("Missing one or more required raw-data files in /raw_data.")
}

main_raw <- read.csv(main_file, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
pre_raw <- read.csv(pre_file, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
page_raw <- read.csv(page_file, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

movie_meta <- tibble::tribble(
  ~movie_title, ~movie_category, ~movie_content, ~movie_side,
  "Silicon Circus", "Political -- Left (Immigration / undocumented workers)", "political", "left",
  "Broken Care", "Political -- Left (Universal healthcare / medical debt)", "political", "left",
  "The Watchers", "Political -- Neutral (Surveillance and privacy)", "political", "neutral",
  "Glory Before Dawn", "Political -- Right (Borders and security)", "political", "right",
  "Divided We Stand", "Political -- Right (Tradition and authority)", "political", "right",
  "Incident in the Dark", "Control -- Non-political (Industrial accident)", "non-political", "non_political",
  "In the Shadows", "Control -- Non-political (Criminal hunt)", "non-political", "non_political",
  "Scandals & Secrets", "Control -- Non-political (Celebrity scandal / media pressure)", "non-political", "non_political",
  "System Failure", "Control -- Non-political (Tech malfunction)", "non-political", "non_political",
  "Beta Launch", "Control -- Non-political (Tech satire / corporate culture)", "non-political", "non_political"
)

parse_pol_answers <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x)) {
    return(list())
  }
  fromJSON(x, simplifyVector = TRUE)
}

mean_or_na <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  mean(x)
}

complete_codes <- main_raw %>%
  mutate(has_decision = nzchar(player.decision)) %>%
  group_by(participant.code) %>%
  summarise(n_decisions = sum(has_decision), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_decisions == 10) %>%
  pull(participant.code)

pre_analysis <- pre_raw %>%
  filter(participant.code %in% complete_codes) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    pol_answers = list(parse_pol_answers(player.pol_answers_json)),
    abortion = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(pol_answers[["women"]])),
    immigration = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(pol_answers[["immigration"]])),
    climate = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(pol_answers[["climate_change"]])),
    # Higher values indicate a more right-leaning profile on the issue items.
    ideology_issue_right = mean(c(7 - abortion, immigration, 7 - climate), na.rm = TRUE),
    ideology_group = case_when(
      ideology_issue_right < 3.5 ~ "left",
      ideology_issue_right > 3.5 ~ "right",
      TRUE ~ "center"
    ),
    treatment_match = if_else(player.treatment_heterogeneous == "yes", "heterogeneous", "homogeneous"),
    treatment_domain = if_else(player.treatment_political == "yes", "political", "neutral"),
    treatment_label = paste(treatment_match, treatment_domain, sep = "_")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(
    participant.code,
    treatment_match,
    treatment_domain,
    treatment_label,
    ideology_issue_right,
    ideology_group
  )

main_analysis <- main_raw %>%
  filter(participant.code %in% complete_codes, nzchar(player.decision)) %>%
  transmute(
    participant.code,
    round_number = as.integer(subsession.round_number),
    decision = player.decision,
    rated = player.decision == "rate",
    movie_rating = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(player.movie_rating)),
    movie_title = player.movie_title,
    treatment_match = if_else(player.treatment_heterogeneous == "yes", "heterogeneous", "homogeneous"),
    treatment_domain = if_else(player.treatment_political == "yes", "political", "neutral"),
    treatment_label = paste(treatment_match, treatment_domain, sep = "_")
  ) %>%
  left_join(movie_meta, by = "movie_title") %>%
  left_join(
    pre_analysis,
    by = c("participant.code", "treatment_match", "treatment_domain", "treatment_label")
  )

page_analysis <- page_raw %>%
  filter(participant_code %in% complete_codes) %>%
  arrange(participant_code, as.integer(page_index), as.numeric(epoch_time_completed)) %>%
  group_by(participant_code) %>%
  mutate(
    prev_epoch = lag(as.numeric(epoch_time_completed)),
    decision_time_sec = as.numeric(epoch_time_completed) - prev_epoch
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(app_name == "main", page_name == "RatingDecision") %>%
  transmute(
    participant.code = participant_code,
    round_number = as.integer(round_number),
    decision_time_sec
  )

decision_level <- main_analysis %>%
  left_join(page_analysis, by = c("participant.code", "round_number")) %>%
  arrange(participant.code, round_number)

participant_level <- decision_level %>%
  group_by(
    participant.code,
    treatment_match,
    treatment_domain,
    treatment_label,
    ideology_issue_right,
    ideology_group
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    movies_rated = sum(rated),
    rate_share = mean(rated),
    mean_rating_given = mean_or_na(movie_rating[rated]),
    mean_decision_time_sec = mean_or_na(decision_time_sec),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

overall_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  metric = c(
    "Participants in pre-experimental file",
    "Participants who completed all 10 main rounds",
    "Share of recruited participants who completed all 10 main rounds",
    "Mean movies rated per completer",
    "Median movies rated per completer",
    "Mean rating probability across all decisions",
    "Mean decision time (seconds)",
    "Median decision time (seconds)"
  ),
  value = c(
    n_distinct(pre_raw$participant.code),
    n_distinct(participant_level$participant.code),
    sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * n_distinct(participant_level$participant.code) / n_distinct(pre_raw$participant.code)),
    sprintf("%.2f", mean(participant_level$movies_rated)),
    sprintf("%.2f", median(participant_level$movies_rated)),
    sprintf("%.2f", mean(decision_level$rated)),
    sprintf("%.2f", mean(decision_level$decision_time_sec, na.rm = TRUE)),
    sprintf("%.2f", median(decision_level$decision_time_sec, na.rm = TRUE))
  )
)

treatment_summary <- participant_level %>%
  group_by(treatment_label, treatment_match, treatment_domain) %>%
  summarise(
    n_participants = n(),
    mean_movies_rated = mean(movies_rated),
    sd_movies_rated = sd(movies_rated),
    mean_rate_share = mean(rate_share),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(treatment_domain, treatment_match)

factor_summary <- bind_rows(
  participant_level %>%
    group_by(factor = "match_type", level = treatment_match) %>%
    summarise(
      n_participants = n(),
      mean_movies_rated = mean(movies_rated),
      sd_movies_rated = sd(movies_rated),
      mean_rate_share = mean(rate_share),
      .groups = "drop"
    ),
  participant_level %>%
    group_by(factor = "domain", level = treatment_domain) %>%
    summarise(
      n_participants = n(),
      mean_movies_rated = mean(movies_rated),
      sd_movies_rated = sd(movies_rated),
      mean_rate_share = mean(rate_share),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
)

content_summary <- decision_level %>%
  group_by(movie_content, movie_side) %>%
  summarise(
    n_decisions = n(),
    rate_probability = mean(rated),
    mean_rating_if_rated = mean_or_na(movie_rating[rated]),
    mean_decision_time_sec = mean_or_na(decision_time_sec),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(movie_content, movie_side)

ideology_content_summary <- decision_level %>%
  filter(ideology_group %in% c("left", "right"), movie_side %in% c("left", "right")) %>%
  group_by(ideology_group, movie_side) %>%
  summarise(
    n_decisions = n(),
    rate_probability = mean(rated),
    mean_rating_if_rated = mean_or_na(movie_rating[rated]),
    mean_decision_time_sec = mean_or_na(decision_time_sec),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(ideology_group, movie_side)

round_summary <- decision_level %>%
  group_by(round_number) %>%
  summarise(
    n_decisions = n(),
    rate_probability = mean(rated),
    mean_decision_time_sec = mean_or_na(decision_time_sec),
    median_decision_time_sec = median(decision_time_sec, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

round_treatment_summary <- decision_level %>%
  group_by(round_number, treatment_label) %>%
  summarise(
    n_decisions = n(),
    rate_probability = mean(rated),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

time_side_summary <- decision_level %>%
  filter(ideology_group %in% c("left", "right"), movie_side %in% c("left", "right")) %>%
  group_by(ideology_group, movie_side) %>%
  summarise(
    n_decisions = n(),
    mean_decision_time_sec = mean_or_na(decision_time_sec),
    median_decision_time_sec = median(decision_time_sec, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

write.csv(participant_level, "pilot_raw_participant_level.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(decision_level, "pilot_raw_decision_level.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(treatment_summary, "pilot_raw_treatment_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(round_summary, "pilot_raw_round_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

This report uses `r basename(main_file)`, `r basename(pre_file)`, and `r basename(page_file)` from `/raw_data`.

The analysis follows the hypotheses summarized in `/text/presentation_BEEN.tex`:

- `H1`: participants should contribute less in homogeneous than heterogeneous matches.
- `H2`: that heterogeneous-homogeneous gap should be larger in the political domain.
- `H3`: contribution should differ for political versus non-political movie content.

All main analyses below use the `r n_distinct(participant_level$participant.code)` participants who completed all 10 main rounds. The pre-experimental file contains `r n_distinct(pre_raw$participant.code)` recruited participants in total, so the completion share is `r sprintf('%.1f%%', 100 * n_distinct(participant_level$participant.code) / n_distinct(pre_raw$participant.code))`.

The raw export does not contain a usable direct left-right self-placement item in this pilot. The ideology sections therefore use a derived issue-based right-leaning score built from three political statements in the pre-treatment survey:

- abortion rights, reverse-coded
- immigration restriction
- climate-priority, reverse-coded

Higher values indicate a more right-leaning issue profile.

## Sample Overview

```{r}
kable(overall_summary, col.names = c("Metric", "Value"), align = c("l", "r"))
```

## How Many Movies Do People Rate?

### Overall Distribution

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
ggplot(participant_level, aes(x = movies_rated)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, boundary = -0.5, fill = "#3b6f8c", color = "white") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:10) +
  labs(
    x = "Movies rated out of 10",
    y = "Participants",
    title = "How many movies participants chose to rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

```{r}
movies_rated_distribution <- participant_level %>%
  count(movies_rated, name = "participants") %>%
  mutate(share = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * participants / sum(participants)))

kable(movies_rated_distribution, col.names = c("Movies rated", "Participants", "Share"), align = c("r", "r", "r"))
```

### Variation Across the Four Treatment Cells

```{r}
kable(
  treatment_summary %>%
    mutate(
      mean_movies_rated = round(mean_movies_rated, 2),
      sd_movies_rated = round(sd_movies_rated, 2),
      mean_rate_share = round(mean_rate_share, 3)
    ),
  col.names = c("Treatment", "Match type", "Domain", "N", "Mean movies rated", "SD", "Mean rate share"),
  align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=4.8}
ggplot(treatment_summary, aes(x = reorder(treatment_label, mean_movies_rated), y = mean_movies_rated, fill = treatment_domain)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Mean movies rated",
    title = "Movies rated by treatment cell"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("neutral" = "#8fb339", "political" = "#cf5c36"), name = "Domain")
```

### Variation Across the Two Treatment Factors

```{r}
kable(
  factor_summary %>%
    mutate(
      mean_movies_rated = round(mean_movies_rated, 2),
      sd_movies_rated = round(sd_movies_rated, 2),
      mean_rate_share = round(mean_rate_share, 3)
    ),
  col.names = c("Factor", "Level", "N", "Mean movies rated", "SD", "Mean rate share"),
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

## Political Versus Non-Political Movie Content

This section speaks most directly to `H3`.

```{r}
kable(
  content_summary %>%
    mutate(
      rate_probability = round(rate_probability, 3),
      mean_rating_if_rated = round(mean_rating_if_rated, 2),
      mean_decision_time_sec = round(mean_decision_time_sec, 2)
    ),
  col.names = c("Movie content", "Movie side", "Decisions", "Rate probability", "Mean rating if rated", "Mean decision time (sec)"),
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=4.8}
ggplot(content_summary, aes(x = movie_side, y = rate_probability, fill = movie_content)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  labs(
    x = "Movie type",
    y = "Probability of choosing rate",
    title = "Rate probability by movie content"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("non-political" = "#8fb339", "political" = "#cf5c36"), name = "Content")
```

## Do Left-Wing Participants Rate Left-Wing Movies More Often or More Positively?

This is descriptive only. The ideology grouping is derived from issue positions, not from a direct self-placement item, because that field is blank in this pilot export. The right-leaning group is small, so these comparisons should be read cautiously.

```{r}
ideology_group_counts <- participant_level %>%
  count(ideology_group, name = "participants") %>%
  arrange(ideology_group)

kable(ideology_group_counts, col.names = c("Ideology group", "Participants"), align = c("l", "r"))
```

```{r}
kable(
  ideology_content_summary %>%
    mutate(
      rate_probability = round(rate_probability, 3),
      mean_rating_if_rated = round(mean_rating_if_rated, 2),
      mean_decision_time_sec = round(mean_decision_time_sec, 2)
    ),
  col.names = c("Participant ideology", "Movie side", "Decisions", "Rate probability", "Mean rating if rated", "Mean decision time (sec)"),
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

```{r fig.width=9, fig.height=4.8}
ggplot(ideology_content_summary, aes(x = movie_side, y = rate_probability, fill = ideology_group)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  labs(
    x = "Movie side",
    y = "Probability of choosing rate",
    title = "Rate probability for left- and right-coded movies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("left" = "#3b6f8c", "right" = "#cf5c36"), name = "Participant ideology")
```

```{r fig.width=9, fig.height=4.8}
ggplot(ideology_content_summary, aes(x = movie_side, y = mean_rating_if_rated, fill = ideology_group)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  labs(
    x = "Movie side",
    y = "Mean rating among rated movies",
    title = "Conditional star ratings for left- and right-coded movies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("left" = "#3b6f8c", "right" = "#cf5c36"), name = "Participant ideology")
```

## How Does Rating Probability Change from Movie 1 to Movie 10?

```{r}
kable(
  round_summary %>%
    mutate(
      rate_probability = round(rate_probability, 3),
      mean_decision_time_sec = round(mean_decision_time_sec, 2),
      median_decision_time_sec = round(median_decision_time_sec, 2)
    ),
  col.names = c("Round", "Decisions", "Rate probability", "Mean decision time (sec)", "Median decision time (sec)"),
  align = c("r", "r", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=4.8}
ggplot(round_summary, aes(x = round_number, y = rate_probability)) +
  geom_line(color = "#3b6f8c", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "#3b6f8c", size = 2.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(
    x = "Shown movie number",
    y = "Probability of choosing rate",
    title = "How rating probability evolves across the 10 rounds"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

## Does the Over-Time Pattern Vary Across Treatments?

This section is the most relevant descriptive check for `H1` and `H2`.

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=5.6}
ggplot(round_treatment_summary, aes(x = round_number, y = rate_probability, color = treatment_label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(
    x = "Shown movie number",
    y = "Probability of choosing rate",
    color = "Treatment",
    title = "Round-by-round rate probability by treatment cell"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

```{r}
round_treatment_wide <- round_treatment_summary %>%
  mutate(rate_probability = round(rate_probability, 3)) %>%
  select(round_number, treatment_label, rate_probability) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = treatment_label, values_from = rate_probability) %>%
  arrange(round_number)

kable(round_treatment_wide, col.names = c("Round", names(round_treatment_wide)[-1]), align = "r")
```

## How Much Time per Decision Do People Spend from Movie 1 to Movie 10?

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=4.8}
ggplot(round_summary, aes(x = round_number)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_decision_time_sec, color = "Mean"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(y = mean_decision_time_sec, color = "Mean"), size = 2.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = median_decision_time_sec, color = "Median"), linewidth = 1, linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = median_decision_time_sec, color = "Median"), size = 2.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Mean" = "#cf5c36", "Median" = "#3b6f8c")) +
  labs(
    x = "Shown movie number",
    y = "Decision time (seconds)",
    color = "",
    title = "Decision times across rounds"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

The first round includes the transition from the pre-experimental stage into the main task, so it is usually longer than later rounds.

## Do Left-Wing or Right-Wing Participants Spend More Time on Left- or Right-Wing Movies?

The table and figure below use only left-coded and right-coded movies. The timing is the time spent on the decision page, regardless of whether the participant eventually chose `rate` or `skip`.

```{r}
kable(
  time_side_summary %>%
    mutate(
      mean_decision_time_sec = round(mean_decision_time_sec, 2),
      median_decision_time_sec = round(median_decision_time_sec, 2)
    ),
  col.names = c("Participant ideology", "Movie side", "Decisions", "Mean decision time (sec)", "Median decision time (sec)"),
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=4.8}
ggplot(time_side_summary, aes(x = movie_side, y = mean_decision_time_sec, fill = ideology_group)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  labs(
    x = "Movie side",
    y = "Mean decision time (seconds)",
    title = "Decision time for left- and right-coded movies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("left" = "#3b6f8c", "right" = "#cf5c36"), name = "Participant ideology")
```

## Exported Files

This report also writes reusable CSVs to the project root:

- `pilot_raw_participant_level.csv`
- `pilot_raw_decision_level.csv`
- `pilot_raw_treatment_summary.csv`
- `pilot_raw_round_summary.csv`
